header: Doctors and non-medical executives (step 46a). The hospital (M&HS) has two cadres of executives with PARALLEL designations. Checked on the live data, 24 Oct 2026, on the main hospital's 63 executives: medical (40): Director(M&HS) 1, Joint Director 11, Sr. Deputy Director 13, Asst. Director/Sr. Consultant 4, DMO/Consultant 3, ADMO/Specialist 1, Medical Officer 7 managerial (23): Director In-charge 1, Dy. General Manager 1, Asst. General Manager 4, Sr. Manager 12, Dy. Manager 2, Asst. Manager 3 "Dr" at the start of a name: 0 of the 63. The data does NOT carry the title, so I never find a doctor by name: nlq.employees.is_doctor (the medical track OR doctor_override, step 48b) is the signal. Nothing here knows a title: the track comes from the designation table (dg.track), so a new medical title needs no change.

symbols.name: isDoctorQuestion
doc: This is a question about doctors or non-medical executives; only then does the search model get DOCTOR_DOC. I leave every other question's prompt untouched, because the prompt has a size limit.

symbols.name: isQualificationQuestion
doc: A question that names a QUALIFICATION or a LEVEL (DNB, MD, MS, MBBS, B.Tech, MBA, "post graduate", a degree): only then does the model get QUALIFICATION_DOC (the doctor prompt has only about 60 characters of budget to spare, see medicalCadre.selftest.ts). In a doctor question the short letters (MD, MS, DM ...) count; in any other question I count only words that cannot be a designation: NOT "graduate" or "diploma" alone ("Graduate Engineer Trainee", "Diploma Trainee" are designations of the directory).

symbols.name: peopleHeadline
symbols.sig: export function peopleHeadline(total: number, truncated: boolean, people: ReadonlyArray<unknown> | null | undefined): string
doc: This is the first line of a list of people:
- When both cohorts are present (e.g. C&IT with 18 execs and 7 non-execs): "25 people found: 18 executives and 7 non-executives."
- When only executives are present and doctors/non-medical are mixed (main hospital): "63 people found: 40 doctors and 23 non-medical."
- When a single cohort is present with no sub-cadre: "16 people found."
I never give a split to a partly loaded list (more than the page holds): it would count only what is on screen.

behaviours: a doctor question's prompt holds the rule
...and says that a doctor is never found by name
an ordinary question's prompt does not hold it (no cost)
the extra text is modest (under 2200 characters), only for those questions
with the 300 real departments, a doctor question about the main hospital stays within the prompt budget (under 17,000 characters, 1,500 spare for the live designations)
the doctor rule is one block of text that names no person
